title: Voice hardening: words never ahead of the voice; Chrome's Google voices
acceptance: For a voice that reports word boundaries, an atom leaves the screen only once the voice has begun the next atom's first word or ended the segment; a voice that claims boundaries and goes quiet is waited on for at most a bounded patience, then estimated; unit-tested.
The first utterance of a reading has a longer grace to begin than later ones, so a cold speech engine does not stand the speech clock down for the whole reading; unit-tested.

Chrome's Google voices are chosen after natural voices and before the default, and are spoken a sentence at a time so the fourteen-second cutoff never applies; one start, one end and sentence marks to listeners; unit-tested.
Owner or a second reader on Chrome on Windows hears a Google voice, and sees no phrase pass faster than it is spoken, on the live release.

evidence.note: Owner, 2026-10-08, on a friend's Chrome PC in Claude: some phrases flashed past faster than the voice, which then caught up; and the voice fell back to the default browser voice.

Merged as ddba7419 (main CI run 37760303919 succeeded): words never ahead of a voice reporting boundaries, a longer first grace, Chrome's Google voices a sentence at a time. Unit tests in src/live/speech-governor.test.js, src/live/speech-governor.guard.test.js and src/live/voices/browser.test.js (criteria 1 to 3).

Merged as 907ab61b (main CI run 37842101050 succeeded): voice hardening 2, the clock after a hold, a voice taken from outside, and the reading that ends when the voice has; findings in docs/product/discussions/2026-10-08-voice-hardening-2-findings.md.
Live release: https://rise.syberlabs.io/release.txt read 3b43a3be on 2026-10-09, after main CI run 37876662647 (CI and production succeeded). It contains ddba7419 (#515) and 907ab61b (#535).

Owner, 2026-10-09, in Claude on the deployed build: "Beautiful!! Much more robust and working well on the voice side. Card behavior still needs further testing from brand new sessions." Not recorded as criterion 4: it does not say Chrome on Windows, a Google voice, or no phrase faster than spoken.

Owner, 2026-10-11, About panel on Edge 155 (Windows) with Microsoft Ava Online (Natural): beat-19 said, beat-20 never began, voice.degraded voice-did-not-start; after a seek back it failed the same way again.

Open on branch voice-utterance-fallback (1c9a4680): a passage a network voice never begins is retried once a sentence at a time before the clock stands down; passages over 600 characters are said in sentences on network voices; About names the passage, its length and the retry. Reproduced in src/live/voice-never-starts.test.js; not yet heard on a real Edge.

Owner, 2026-10-11, field trace on Edge (Windows) with Microsoft Ava Online (Natural), a stored premium-educational card: speech.end beat-22 at 108.211 s, then run.finished at 112.281 s and no speech between; asked whether the last atom was meant to be narrated.

Open on branch last-beat-spoken (0f03cfe2): tests only. The 4 s is premium-educational's closing shown line (show + hold 3,500 ms, said by no one by the style's design) and the seam before it; the runtime reproduces 4,063 ms. src/live/last-beat.test.js pins that the last beat with words is said whole before run.finished (sealed v1 and v2, streamed, synthetic and late-starting browser voices), plus card and venue e2e. No defect found; not yet heard on a real Edge.

activity.summary: Opened from the owner's second-PC witness in Claude; design approved by the owner the same day.
Reconciled: shipped as #515 (ddba7419), hardened by #535 (907ab61b), both in live release 3b43a3be; delivery deployed, in review for the Chrome-on-Windows human gate
network voice: a passage that never starts is retried sentence-wise before the voice is given up on; long passages are spoken sentence-wise on network voices
field trace: a premium-educational reading's last 4 s of silence is its closing shown line by design; the last beat with words is pinned as said whole before the reading ends (#630)

summary: Hardens the browser voice as the reading's clock: the words on screen wait for the word spoken, a cold engine gets a longer first grace, and Chrome readers get a Google voice spoken a sentence at a time.
blocker: Criterion 4 is a human gate: the owner or a second reader on Chrome on Windows hears a Google voice and sees no phrase pass faster than it is spoken, on the live release.
